  • PURPOSE:
    • To provide protocol on appropriate cleaning, disinfection and sterilization of patient care items and the hospital environment.
  • SCOPE:
    • Hospital Wide – All Inpatient care areas
  • RESPONSIBILTY:
    • Consultants / Doctors
    • All hospital staff
    • Patients
    • Visitors
  • ABBREVIATION:
    • NABH: National Accreditation Board For Hospitals and Healthcare providers
    • HIC: Hospital Infection Control
  • DEFINITION:
    • Sterilization: Complete removal or destruction of all forms of microbial life, including bacteria, viruses, fungi and spores. Principal sterilizing agents are steam under pressure, dry heat, ethylene oxide gas, hydrogen peroxide gas plasma and liquid chemicals. Chemicals used to destroy all microbial life, including fungal and bacterial spores, are called chemo sterilizers.
    • Disinfection: Removal or destruction of pathogenic micro- organisms, with the exception of spores, on inanimate objects. Some disinfectants such as 2.0% gluteraldehyde [cidex] will kill spores when used with long exposure times [10 hrs].
    • Cleaning: is the removal of all foreign material such as soil and organic matter from surfaces. Cleaning is normally done using water, soap detergent or vacuum. Cleaning must precede disinfection or sterilization.
    • Decontamination: The removal of pathogenic micro- organisms from objects so that they are safe to handle.
    • Germicide: Anything, which destroys microorganisms, particularly pathogenic organisms. Usually refers to chemicals, which will destroy pathogens but not necessarily spores. Germicides apply to compounds used on both living tissue and inanimate objects while disinfectants are applied to inanimate objects. Similar terms are bactericide, fungicide, virucide, tuberclocide and sporicide.
    • Antiseptic: A chemical used externally or on the skin or in and around wounds in order to control surface microbial contamination, which could cause infection.
  • REFERENCE:
    • NABH: NABH.
    • HIC: The organization adheres to cleaning, disinfection and sterilization practices.
    • HIC: There are documented policies and procedures for sterilization activities in the organization..
  • POLICY:
    • General Principles:
      • All items shall be thoroughly rinsed after disinfecting. Care shall be taken not to re-contaminate the items.
      • Only surfaces in direct contact with the germicidal solution shall be opened disassembled and completely submerged for the required period of time.
      • Items shall be dry before submerging to avoid diluting the solution to inactive level.
      • Disinfectants are designed for inanimate objects and are damaging to skin. Gloves shall be worn to protect hands. Goggles shall be worn to protect the eyes from splashes. Generally the more effective against microbes the more toxic to humans.
      • All containers used for cleaning agents, disinfectants and other chemicals shall be properly labeled as to contents and expiry date, if applicable.
      • Disinfectants shall be used in well – ventilated rooms.
    • Processing Patient Care Equipment Contaminated With HIV or HBV: For instruments or devices contaminated with blood or body fluids from patients infected with Human Immunodeficiency Vireos (HIV), Hepatitis B virus (HBV) or with respiratory secretions from a patient with pulmonary Tuberculosis (TB). HIV, HBV and TB organisms shall be inactivated by commonly used chemical germicides. Standard sterilization and disinfection procedures for patient care equipment shall be followed.
    • Blood Spills: Cleaning up spills is the responsibility of all HOSPITAL personnel. Individuals cleaning up spills of blood, body fluids and unknown substances shall wear disposable gloves and use equipment to prevent skin injury / contamination. Pour Lysoformin 2%/equivalent solution over the spill appropriate to the size, and wait for 10mts and then wipe clean.
    • Classification of instruments & patient care items:
      • Semi-critical items: These will come into contact with mucous membranes or with skin that is not intact. They must be free of all microorganisms except bacterial spores. Intact mucous membranes are generally resistant to infection by common bacterial spores but are susceptible to tubercle bacilli and viruses. Respiratory therapy and anesthesia equipment, gastrointestinal endoscopes, vaginal specula, cystoscopes, urinary catheters and thermometers are in this category. Semi critical items require high-level disinfection using wet pasteurization or chemical germicides. These items shall be rinsed with sterile water or with tap water with at least 10ppm chlorine after disinfection.
      • Non- critical items: These items come into contact with intact skin but not mucous membranes. Intact skin acts as an effective barrier to most organisms and sterility is not critical. Bedpans, blood pressure cuffs, crutches, bed rails, linen, some food utensils, bedside tables and patient furniture are examples of non-critical items. Depending on the particular item and the nature and the degree of contamination during use, simple washing or scrubbing with a detergent and warm water may be sufficient. In some instances, however, the added assurance of chemical disinfection with an intermediate to low level chemical germicide shall be considered appropriate.
    • Sterilisation and Disinfection of Items:
ITEMSSTANDARD PROCEDURE
AirwaySingle use: Disposable.
Non disposable shall be washed with running water and Cleaning: with Bodedex® forte’s 0.5 % - 1 %, exposure time 5 - 10 minutes. Afterwards clean with normal saline and dry
Ambu bagsIn case of Emergency - After every use to be cleaned with running water and dip in Bodedex® forte’s 0.5 % - 1 %, exposure time 5 - 10 minutes . Wash with running water and dry it before use .
For ETO , Clean the bag with rectified spirit and send for ETO.
Bed and bed cotWash with 0.5% Benzolkonium chloride
Bedding and clothingPlace in appropriate laundry bag.
Soiled or contaminated with blood and body fluids to be placed it in a yellow plastic bag and labeled and tied effectively.
If the linen is from the isolation room place in the yellow bag and label it as infected linen and tie it effectively.
Bed side tablesWet Dusting with 0.5% Benzolkonium chloride
Bed pans / urinalsDisposables are recommended.
If non disposable bedpans and urinals, wear non sterile gloves and apron, wash in bed pan with soap and water and afterwards wash with 0.5% Benzolkonium chloride after drying, formaline tables are placed for 3hours, before use it need to be cleaned with water .
The bed pan holder shall be thoroughly washed with detergent and water and dried.
If viral infection is suspected use sodium hypochlorite 1% For 1hour
Electric FansWipe with detergent and water weekly once
Extractor ventsWipe weekly with detergent and water maintained by maintenance department.
Environment and floor
a. Dry clean
b. Wet clean
c. Terminal cleaning		No brooms to be used. Dust control mop, wash with soap water after every use. Vacuum filters changed when visibly dirty and at least every month.
Use detergent and water with frequent changes
Clean with separate mop and detergent. All horizontal surfaces shall be thoroughly cleaned and dried using disposable clothes.
CorridorsFloor/ Corridors shall be cleaned with 0.5% Benzalkonium chloride
Cleaning is done 2times in 24 hours and whenever required
CasualtyFloor/ Corridors shall be cleaned with 0.5% Benzalkonium chloride
Cleaning is done 2 times in 24 hours and whenever required
Wards / OPD/ Administrative officeFloor/ Corridors shall be cleaned with Phenol and water 1:25
Cleaning is done 2times in 24 hours and whenever required
Suction JarAfter suction the contents need to be discarded into the wash basin (allocated for discarding liquid waste) after treating with 2 % Hypochlorite solution.
Wash with running water and treat with Hydrogen peroxide 3% wait for 3minutes then wash under running water and use.
SuturesIdeally suture should not be re-used
Re use can be done for the same patient The suture should soak in the 2% Glutaraldehyde Cidex at least for a period of 10 minutes. After which it should be soaked for few seconds in the sterile water solution to remove all the Cidex.
Hands
A. Social hand wash		Wash hands with Dettol solution
Before starting work
Before leaving the work
Before handling food and drugs
After handling patients and beddings
After handling bedpans urinals or contaminated equipments
After using toilets
Whenever hands are contaminated
B. Aseptic wash
C. hand wash		Wash with Povione iodine/ 20 % Chlorhexidine solution
Use before carrying an aseptic technique, Before entering an isolation room
Before leaving the isolation room
Before and after care of any immunocompromised patient.
Before surgical procedure in operation theater.
Mattresses, pillows and other cloth itemsMattress and pillows to be cleaned with 3 % Hydrogen Peroxide. If the pillow is wet with blood or body fluids must be washed under running water and then it will be cleaned with 2% Hypochlorite solution wait for 15 mins then wash with water dry and use.
Nail brushSingle use
RazorsUse disposable one
Shaving brushesSingle use
InstrumentsAll items should be drained of fluids such as blood urine or body fluids and rinse thoroughly disinfect with Bodedex forte 0.5% solution before sending for sterilization.
All sharps, Scalpel blades to be removed and disposed at user level into a designated sharp container.
Minor Surgery Instruments like Scissors, Forceps, thumb forceps ,needle , BP Handle with knife etc after cleaning with running water shall be dipped in 2% Glutaraldehyde (Cidex) for 8 hours and then washed 3 times with sterile water, kept in the sterile trays.
Instruments from known infected patients should be wrapped, labeled separately. Wash under running water then clean with Bodedex forte 1% for 5mins and wash with running water afterwards send for autoclave
Skin preparation for injectionsWipe with 70% alcohol
Sphygmomanometer cuffWash weekly with soap solution
If used for infected patient use single or use plastic cover and wipe with 70% alcohol
StethoscopeClean at regular intervals with Bodedex Forte 0.5 % solution, and if visibly contaminated wipe with 70% alcohol.
Use separate stethoscope for the isolation patient.
Suction equipmentAll suction equipment should be stored clean and dry
All suction catheter should be single use
Suction jar must be cleaned every 24 hrs and after every use and between patients. Discard all the contents in the wash basin (dedicated one) with 2% Hypochlorite solution then Clean jar in the running water and with Bodedex forte solution 1% for 5 min then it can be used
TelephoneWipe with 70% alcohol daily
Thermometer
Oral
Rectal		Wash with running water and wipe with 70% alcohol swab after each use, store dry.
Wash with running water wipe with 70% alcohol soak with Bodedex forte solution 0.5% after each use.
Trolleys
Dressing
Patients trolley		Wash with detergent wipe with 70% alcohol before and after procedure. Trolley surface must be dry before placing sterile items.
Wash with water and detergent. If soiled during use, clean with Bodedex forte solution 0.5% . Keep clean and dry.
Sputum cupsSingle use , Alternative wash under running water then treat with Bodedex forte solution 0.5% for 5 min then wash with water and keep Formalin tablets for 3 hrs. Before patient use wash with water.
Ward curtainsCurtains should be changed and washed when dirty or when the patient is discharged.
Urine drainage bagsClosed system must be maintained to reduce risk of introducing microorganisms. Discard after patient use
  • Cleaning of Infected Room:
        • Linen should be stripped from the bed taking care not to shake the linen during this action. The linen should be bagged properly before being sent to the laundry in a leak-proof bag.
        • All other articles like IV stands and furniture should be cleaned with detergent and disinfected with 2 percent bacillocid.
        • Walls should be cleaned with detergent and disinfected with 2 percent bacillocid.
        • Bathrooms should be cleaned with detergent and disinfected with phenol.
    • The Recall procedure:
      • The sterilization process is regularly monitored. Records maintained to indicate Machine number, Batch number, Contents of batch, temperature, pressure, Date of sterilization, Date of expiry, etc.
      • Whenever a particular sterilized pack kept in storage is found open / not usable, the same is tracked to find out the date of sterilization and the batch so that all those items belonging to the particular batch & machine are identified & recalled back for re-sterilization.

STORAGE OF STERILE ITEMS

General Requirements

  • Sterile items must be stored in a clean, dry, well-ventilated, and dust-free environment
  • Access to sterile storage areas should be restricted to authorized personnel only
  • Storage area must be physically separated from dirty/contaminated zones

Environmental Conditions

  • Temperature: Maintain as per hospital policy (ideally 20–24°C)
  • Humidity: Below 60%
  • Avoid direct sunlight and moisture exposure

Storage Practices

  • Store items on:
    • Closed cabinets or covered racks
    • Shelves at least:
      • 8–10 inches above floor
      • 2 inches away from walls
      • Below ceiling level
  • Do not overcrowd shelves
  • Maintain proper spacing for air circulation

Arrangement & Stock Rotation

  • Follow FIFO (First In First Out) principle
  • Label each pack clearly with:
    • Date of sterilization
    • Expiry date
    • Batch number
  • Separate sterile and non-sterile items clearly

Shelf Life & Integrity

  • Shelf life depends on:
    • Type of packaging
    • Storage conditions
  • Before use, check:
    • Integrity of pack (no tears, moisture, or damage)
    • Expiry date
    • Chemical indicator status
  • Any compromised pack must be reprocessed immediately

Handling of Sterile Items

  • Perform hand hygiene before handling
  • Use clean hands or sterile gloves
  • Avoid excessive handling
  • Do not place sterile packs on floor or contaminated surfaces

ISSUE OF STERILE ITEMS

4.1 Authorization

  • Sterile items are issued only against:
    • Proper requisition slip
    • Indent form or electronic request
  • Requests must be approved by authorized personnel

Issue Procedure

  • Verify:
    • Item name and quantity
    • Department request
  • Check:
    • Sterility (intact packaging, indicator status)
    • Expiry date
  • Record details in issue register/software:
    • Date and time
    • Item issued
    • Quantity
    • Batch/lot number
    • Issued to (department/person)

Transportation

  • Transport sterile items in:
    • Clean, covered, and dedicated trolleys/containers
  • Avoid mixing sterile and contaminated items
  • Protect from:
    • Dust
    • Moisture
    • Physical damage

Handling at Receiving Area

  • Receiving staff must:
    • Verify integrity of packs
    • Check expiry and indicators
  • Store immediately in designated sterile area

Return of Unused Items

  • Accept only if:
    • Pack is intact and unopened
    • Within expiry
  • Reinspect before restocking
  • If compromised → send for re-sterilization

Management of Expired/Damaged Items

  • Do not issue expired items
  • Segregate and label as “Not for Use”
  • Send for reprocessing
